entry.title: Summer Replay: The Energetic Sound of Ersin Secrin
entry.summary: N ever has there been a time where a beat was not associated with some kind of a story or experience. There comes an upcoming artist with a music that brings you back to summer days in just one listen. This is the case for…
entry.content:
N ever has there been a time where a beat was not associated with some kind of a story or experience. There comes an upcoming artist with a music that brings you back to summer days in just one listen. This is the case for Ersin Secrin who is coming up with a new pop song, entitled "Replay".

In today's music market, artists are looking to bring something different that will captivate their audiences' attention and make them enjoy the piece of work. Ersin Secrin's "Replay" is an example of such a song, full of energy and intended to take over the listeners' hearts and make them move around.

The core theme of "Replay" by Ersin Secrin lies in the ideas of fun and freedom that are associated with summertime. For him, such a mood should reflect in the creation and it is why he has created a pop song that is full of fun and positive vibes. With this song, one is bound to forget all worries and simply enjoy the sounds of it.



Ersin Secrin is not just a songwriter, but also a producer who knows how to create experiences for his audiences. This can be seen with his latest song entitled "Replay". It is full of dynamism and exciting music which makes it possible to enjoy it at every point.

"Replay" is a track that has everything for summer scenarios. It is a perfect song that can be played at beach clubs, streets or car playlist during driving on the highway. It has a rhythm that is bound to make the dance floor move and it will also make the listeners hum along.

What makes Ersin's music different from other artists' music is the fact that in it there are no unnecessary words. He is capable of creating music tracks that express certain emotions and ideas of a story in a way that is comprehensible for listeners.

It seems that music by Ersin Secrin is contemporary and timeless at the same time. He is interested in making his pieces of art inspire people and help them feel something. That is why with "Replay", people will surely find out that there is so much that this track offers.

Ersin's music is expected to become even more popular since his latest single is about to start conquering the playlists.

entry.title: Spotify Boosts Share Repurchase Program
entry.summary: Spotify has expanded its share repurchase program by an additional $1.5 billion, bringing the total authorization to approximately $2.223 billion, according to a press release issued on Thursday (August 20). The company’s Board of Directors approved the increase. With $723 million remaining under the existing…
entry.content:
Spotify has expanded its share repurchase program by an additional $1.5 billion, bringing the total authorization to approximately $2.223 billion, according to a press release issued on Thursday (August 20). The company’s Board of Directors approved the increase.

With $723 million remaining under the existing program, Spotify now has nearly double the initial authorization announced in 2021 when it was granted up to $1.0 billion for repurchasing ordinary shares. A further expansion to $1.0 billion was authorized by shareholders in July 2025.

Spotify clarified that the timing and number of shares bought back will depend on factors such as renewal of shareholder authorization, market conditions, and alternative investment opportunities. The company stated it can engage in share repurchases through various methods, including open market purchases, subject to US Securities and Exchange Commission rules.

While Spotify is not alone among large-scale music industry players in undertaking share buybacks, the firm has been active in this area. Universal Music Group launched its first-ever share buyback program worth €500 million ($575m) in March and doubled that authorization to €1 billion by August. UMG used half of the expanded authorization to purchase shares from Bill Ackman’s Pershing Square, which sold Spotify after rejecting a $64 billion takeover bid.

UMG completed its initial €500 million program in July, having spent €499.2 million buying back its own stock. The company is now launching an additional €250 million tranche of the program.

Spotify has been actively expanding its share base as it aims to bolster its financial position and potentially offset declines in subscription revenue. In Q2 2026, Spotify grew its Premium subscriber base by 7 million to reach 300 million paying users, bringing the firm’s total Monthly Active Users (MAUs) across 184 markets to 777 million.

The company reported total revenue of EUR €4.777 billion ($5.56bn) in Q2 2026, up 14% year-over-year, and posted quarterly operating income of €655 million ($762m). At the end of that quarter, Spotify held €9.4 billion in cash, restricted cash, and short-term investments.

entry.title: Apple Music Introduces "Made With AI" Label for AI-Generated Content
entry.summary: Apple Music has introduced a new “Made With AI” label for music generated using artificial intelligence (AI), requiring record labels and distributors to tag such content. The move, announced by Apple in a memo to industry partners on August 20, will make these tags visible…
entry.content:
Apple Music has introduced a new “Made With AI” label for music generated using artificial intelligence (AI), requiring record labels and distributors to tag such content. The move, announced by Apple in a memo to industry partners on August 20, will make these tags visible to listeners later this year.

The requirement comes as part of Apple Music’s ongoing effort to address the growing use of AI in music creation. Since March, the platform has been using AI Transparency Tags to flag AI-generated content across tracks and videos. However, rather than detecting AI content itself, Apple relies on record labels and distributors to include these tags.

This approach contrasts with Spotify’s recent announcement regarding an “AI Persona” badge for artist profiles, which will be reviewed by the company itself in addition to relying on self-disclosed credits. Deezer has also developed its own technology to detect AI-generated tracks and label them accordingly.

The introduction of this new label aligns with broader regulatory requirements set by the EU’s AI Act, which mandates that providers of generative AI systems embed machine-readable markers in their content from August 2 onwards. Suno, one of the services affected, has stated plans to adopt audio watermarking and fingerprinting to help identify and tag AI-generated tracks.

As the music industry grapples with the implications of AI-generated content, Apple’s move underscores its commitment to transparency and regulation compliance. The introduction of the “Made With AI” label is expected to provide clearer identification for these tracks across streaming platforms, facilitating better tracking and management by record labels and distributors.

entry.title: DJ Matrix Returns From the Underground With a Legacy Built on Bass
entry.summary: Long before the current wave of electronic nostalgia turned old breakbeats into cultural currency, DJ Matrix was already making records designed to move people. In 1986, while serving in the US Marines, he independently released "Feel My Bass," a track that would eventually become closely…
entry.content:
Long before the current wave of electronic nostalgia turned old breakbeats into cultural currency, DJ Matrix was already making records designed to move people. In 1986, while serving in the US Marines, he independently released "Feel My Bass," a track that would eventually become closely associated with breakdance culture and competitions around the world. What began as an independent release became something considerably larger, surviving decades away from the spotlight through the enthusiasm of listeners who continued to share it, discuss it, and keep its memory alive online.

That persistence is at the heart of DJ Matrix's unusual return to music. His career was interrupted when the Gulf War began, bringing his original musical ambitions to an abrupt halt. For many artists, nearly four decades away would represent the end of a story. For Matrix, it turned out to be a pause.

 

The catalyst for his return came from an unexpected source. Egyptian Lover, a foundational figure in electro and West Coast electronic music, went looking for Matrix and eventually persuaded him to step back into the studio. Their collaboration produced "Hypnotic," released on 808 Day, 8 August 2025, and marked the beginning of a second chapter that few could have predicted when "Feel My Bass" first appeared.

There is something particularly satisfying about the way Matrix's comeback has unfolded. It has not been built solely on nostalgia. Instead, the renewed interest in his earlier work has opened the door to new collaborations and fresh music. His partnership with Beat Junkies founder J.Rocc resulted in "Feel My Bass, Reloaded," released on 22 March, a modern reworking of the track that started everything. After years of fans asking for a remake, Matrix finally returned to the song on his own terms, and by his own assessment, the new version surpasses the original.

That confidence is important because the story of DJ Matrix is not simply about recovering a lost moment. It is about discovering what an artist with decades of additional perspective can do with the sound that first gave him a name. "Feel My Bass" belongs to another era, but its continued life among breakdance fans demonstrates that the fundamental appeal of a great rhythm does not disappear with time.

Matrix's music has always been rooted in movement. The connection between his early work and breakdancing was not incidental. "Feel My Bass" became a soundtrack for dancers who needed music with physical impact, the kind of track that gives a routine momentum and makes a room respond. That relationship between sound and movement remains central to the artist's identity as he builds the next stage of his career.

Now, however, the project has expanded. House Of Neo is Matrix's new alter ego and the vehicle through which he is exploring house and dubstep. Rather than attempting to recreate the past indefinitely, the new identity gives him room to explore a different side of electronic music while retaining the instincts that have defined his work for decades.

The first House Of Neo single, "Drift Away," arrived on 5 June and established the new project. Its follow up, "Tension," moves in a noticeably different direction, suggesting that Matrix is interested in variety rather than building the entire project around one predictable formula. That willingness to shift mood and approach is particularly relevant for an artist whose history already stretches across multiple generations of electronic music.

Then there is "Road Trippin' With Angels," a track built around a very different emotional purpose. Where "Tension" introduces a contrasting atmosphere, "Road Trippin' With Angels" is positioned as an uplifting, feel good piece of music made for the open road. It captures another important part of Matrix's musical personality, the ability to make electronic music that is not solely concerned with intensity or club energy, but can also create a sense of freedom and enjoyment.

entry.title: Evil Rabbit Begins Again, One Beat at a Time
entry.summary: The first step into a new creative role can reveal as much about an artist as years of finished work. For Evil Rabbit, that step arrives with "Tender," his first official release as a music producer and the opening single from an upcoming debut mixtape.
entry.content:
The first step into a new creative role can reveal as much about an artist as years of finished work. For Evil Rabbit, that step arrives with "Tender," his first official release as a music producer and the opening single from an upcoming debut mixtape. Having only begun producing less than a year ago, he approaches the track not as a declaration that he has arrived, but as evidence of a process already underway.

That distinction matters. "Tender" comes from an artist still learning the language of production, experimenting with ideas, and discovering how the instincts he developed as a touring drummer can translate into a different kind of musical architecture. Rather than presenting the single as a polished endpoint, Evil Rabbit allows it to represent something more interesting, the beginning of a new chapter built through curiosity, collaboration, and repetition.

His background behind the drum kit provides an important foundation. As a touring drummer, Evil Rabbit has spent years understanding rhythm from the inside, learning how timing, dynamics, space, and physical movement can shape a performance. Production asks for a different kind of listening, but the instincts are connected. Where a drummer once responds to the movement of a band in real time, a producer has the opportunity to construct that movement piece by piece, deciding how every sound contributes to the final atmosphere.

That transition has happened remarkably quickly. Less than a year after stepping into production, Evil Rabbit is already introducing his first official material while building toward a larger body of work. Yet the speed of the progression does not appear to have replaced patience. If anything, "Tender" represents an artist who understands that learning the craft is part of the music itself.

The title carries an intriguing sense of vulnerability for a debut production. "Tender" suggests sensitivity, attention, and a willingness to handle something carefully. In the context of Evil Rabbit's current journey, it feels appropriate. He is entering unfamiliar territory while bringing years of musical experience with him, testing what happens when the drummer's instinct for rhythm becomes part of a broader production process.

Much of the character surrounding the release comes from the creative community he has developed alongside in Tucson. Working with a growing network of artists and creatives has allowed Evil Rabbit to learn through collaboration rather than isolation. That environment becomes particularly important for an emerging producer, where every session can introduce a new approach to arrangement, sound selection, recording, or songwriting.

There is an appealing sense of collective discovery to that process. Evil Rabbit is not presenting himself as an artist operating from a finished blueprint. He is building that blueprint as he goes, learning from the people around him and carrying each experience into the next record. The result is a creative trajectory that feels open ended, with "Tender" functioning as the first visible marker of a much longer road.

His decision to move from performance into production also reflects a natural expansion of musical curiosity. Drumming teaches an artist to understand the importance of groove, but producing requires attention to every layer surrounding it. Texture, atmosphere, arrangement, transitions, and sonic detail all become part of the composition. The challenge is not simply to make a beat work, but to understand why a particular sound belongs there and what happens when it is removed.

For someone with a background in touring, that shift can be especially revealing. Live performance is immediate and physical. Production is more solitary and microscopic, often demanding repeated listening and tiny adjustments that may be invisible to anyone outside the studio. Evil Rabbit's first year in the role has therefore been a period of learning how to move between those two worlds.

"Tender" represents that learning process in real time. It is the first step toward establishing an identity beyond the role of drummer, while still carrying the rhythmic instincts that brought him there in the first place. That connection gives the release a sense of continuity. He is not abandoning one musical identity for another. He is expanding the possibilities of what that identity can become.

The upcoming mixtape promises to make that development easier to trace. Rather than treating "Tender" as a standalone experiment, Evil Rabbit is using it as the beginning of a larger body of work through which he can test ideas, work with other artists, and refine his production instincts. Each release becomes another opportunity to learn, with the mixtape serving as a record of that evolution.

There is something refreshing about an artist being willing to occupy that space. Music culture often places enormous pressure on new artists to arrive fully formed, as though experimentation should happen privately and only the finished product should be presented to an audience. Evil Rabbit takes a different approach. The appeal of his current chapter lies partly in watching the craft develop.

That does not mean ambition is absent. Quite the opposite. The desire to collaborate with more artists and continue improving points toward a long term creative vision. The difference is that Evil Rabbit seems more interested in building something durable than rushing toward a particular destination.

Tucson provides the backdrop for that development, giving him access to a community of musicians and creatives whose influence can become part of the process. Local scenes have always played an important role in shaping distinctive artists, particularly when collaboration happens organically and people are willing to experiment outside established formulas. Evil Rabbit's current work appears to be emerging from exactly that kind of environment.

There is also a certain confidence in calling the first release "Tender." It is not a title that suggests aggression or self importance. Instead, it points toward emotional openness, a quality that can be surprisingly powerful in music made by someone entering a new phase. Production is often associated with control, but "Tender" hints at another side of the discipline, the ability to listen closely enough to know when an idea needs space.

That may ultimately become one of the defining qualities of Evil Rabbit's development. His experience as a drummer has already taught him that rhythm is not simply about playing more. It is about knowing when to strike, when to hold back, and how silence can shape momentum. Those instincts can become equally valuable in production, where restraint and timing often determine whether a track feels alive.

As a first official release, "Tender" is therefore best understood as a beginning rather than a conclusion. It introduces a producer who is still discovering the full extent of his capabilities, but who already has a substantial musical foundation beneath the experimentation. The upcoming mixtape will provide a broader canvas, allowing him to explore what happens when those instincts are pushed further.

For now, the most compelling part of Evil Rabbit's story is its openness. He is learning, collaborating, experimenting, and allowing each record to teach him something that the next one can build upon. "Tender" captures that spirit at an early but significant moment, when the possibilities still seem wide open and every new production choice carries the excitement of discovery.

The track may be the first official marker of Evil Rabbit's life as a producer, but it does not feel like a line drawn under his past. It feels like another door opening. Behind it is a drummer's understanding of rhythm, a new producer's curiosity about sound, and a growing Tucson creative community ready to contribute to the next chapter.

"Tender" is where that journey becomes audible. What comes next will show just how far Evil Rabbit can take it.

entry.title: Cardi B's Solo Single "Ah Ha" Makes Debut After Year-Long Break
entry.summary: New York rapper Cardi B has released a new single titled "Ah Ha," her first solo music since the release of her 2025 album, Am I the Drama?. The track was produced by DJ SwanQo and features Cardi's signature humor and sass. Notably, she includes…
entry.content:
New York rapper Cardi B has released a new single titled "Ah Ha," her first solo music since the release of her 2025 album, Am I the Drama?. The track was produced by DJ SwanQo and features Cardi's signature humor and sass. Notably, she includes the line "na na na boo boo" in the lyrics.

This single marks a return to form for Cardi B after embarking on an arena tour in support of her second album last year. She also performed two songs from the record, including “Bodega Baddie” and “ErrTime,” on Saturday Night Live earlier this year.

The release comes as part of Cardi's ongoing musical career, which has seen her perform alongside other notable artists such as Billie Eilish at Coachella 2021. With "Ah Ha," Cardi appears to be continuing the momentum from her recent success and is likely aiming to solidify her position in the music industry once again.

entry.title: Kanye West faced accusations of using AI in Vultures 2
entry.summary: The producer, whose suit was filed anonymously in Los Angeles’ Superior Court, alleges that he was brought in “on an emergency basis” just two days before Vultures 2’s release. He contends that his work included creating at least 13 custom AI voice models and more…
entry.content:
The producer, whose suit was filed anonymously in Los Angeles’ Superior Court, alleges that he was brought in “on an emergency basis” just two days before Vultures 2’s release. He contends that his work included creating at least 13 custom AI voice models and more than 400 individual vocal generations, based on his own voice. The producer claims to have contributed further AI vocal programming to West's most recent solo album, Bully, starting in October 2024.

His suit alleges he has not yet been paid for his work on both Bully and Vultures 2, nor have he and his label, YZY, included him in the production credits on streaming platforms. He seeks at least $110,000 in breach of contract, unjust enrichment, and violations of California’s Unfair Competition Law and the Los Angeles Freelance Worker Protections Ordinance.

West had previously stated that Bully used no AI technology, despite his acknowledgment of using it in songwriting and recording. Last week, West settled a 2024 lawsuit brought against him by Lauren Pisciotta, who accused him of sexual assault and harassment. Another recent court case involving an uncleared sample on the Donda track "Hurricane" ended in favor of the plaintiff, with West ordered to pay just under $200,000.

Vultures 2 was released in 2024, following allegations of AI manipulation. The producer’s lawsuit brings renewed scrutiny to Kanye West's use of technology in his music production.

entry.title: Karol G Surprises Fans with Bruno Mars Collaboration During Los Angeles Show
entry.summary: During Karol G’s second sold-out show at Los Angeles’ SoFi Stadium, the Colombian superstar brought out her collaborator Bruno Mars for a live performance of their new collaboration, “Still,” from Karol G’s latest studio album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. The track debuted on…
entry.content:
During Karol G’s second sold-out show at Los Angeles’ SoFi Stadium, the Colombian superstar brought out her collaborator Bruno Mars for a live performance of their new collaboration, “Still,” from Karol G’s latest studio album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. The track debuted on Billboard’s Hot 100 in March and features the pair harmonizing about unconditional love despite no longer being together.

The event was notable not only for the performance but also as it marked the filming of “Still”’s music video. Fans were informed through a large video screen that they would be witnessing the song’s official recording right then and there with Karol G and Bruno Mars, who wore matching outfits for added impact.

Karol G opened the power ballad in a sparkling white dress before being joined by Bruno Mars, who sported a flower-embroidered white suit adorned with a cowboy hat. The pair then performed “Still,” the opening track from Bruno Mars’ upcoming album, The Romantic.

The new single has received positive reception, as Karol G revealed she posted a TikTok video discussing it and how it expressed her current emotions naturally without feeling pressured to use another language. "There’s a song on the album that’s entirely in English," she said, emphasizing the importance of organic expression in music creation.
